title: Conjecture 1
statement_text: If $G = (V, E)$ is a connected graph embedded in a fixed surface, then $\mathrm{xc}(P_{\mathrm{sp.trees}}(G)) = O(|V|)$.
context_text: For a connected (simple, finite) graph $G=(V,E)$, the spanning tree polytope $P_{\mathrm{sp.trees}}(G)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^E$ is the convex hull of the characteristic vectors of the spanning trees of $G$. An extended formulation of a polytope $P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ is a linear system $Ax+By\le b$, $Cx+Dy=c$ in variables $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, $y\in\mathbb{R}^k$ such that $P=\{x:\exists y,\ Ax+By\le b,\ Cx+Dy=c\}$; its size is its number of inequalities (equalities are not counted), and the extension complexity $\mathrm{xc}(P)$ is the minimum size of an extended formulation of $P$, equivalently the minimum number of facets of a polytope that affinely projects onto $P$. Known bounds: $\mathrm{xc}(P_{\mathrm{sp.trees}}(G))=O(|V||E|)$ for every connected graph (Wong, Martin), and $O(|V|)$ for connected planar graphs (Williams). Here the genus $g$ of a surface is its number of handles or crosscaps (orientable and non-orientable surfaces are both allowed), and the constant in the $O(\cdot)$ may depend on the surface. The authors prove that $\mathrm{xc}(P_{\mathrm{sp.trees}}(G))=O(g^{1/2}|V|^{3/2}+g^{3/2}|V|^{1/2})$ for connected graphs embedded in a surface of genus $g$, hence $O(|V|^{3/2})$ for fixed $g$ (previously known formulations had size $O(|V|^2+g|V|)$), and conjecture that the linear planar bound extends to every fixed surface.
paper_title: Smaller Extended Formulations for the Spanning Tree Polytope of Bounded-genus Graphs

title: Conjecture 2
statement_text: If $\mathcal{C}$ is a proper minor-closed family of graphs and $G = (V, E)$ is a connected graph in $\mathcal{C}$, then $\mathrm{xc}(P_{\mathrm{sp.trees}}(G)) = O(|V|)$.
context_text: For a connected (simple, finite) graph $G=(V,E)$, the spanning tree polytope $P_{\mathrm{sp.trees}}(G)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^E$ is the convex hull of the characteristic vectors of the spanning trees of $G$. An extended formulation of a polytope $P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ is a linear system $Ax+By\le b$, $Cx+Dy=c$ in variables $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, $y\in\mathbb{R}^k$ such that $P=\{x:\exists y,\ Ax+By\le b,\ Cx+Dy=c\}$; its size is its number of inequalities (equalities are not counted), and the extension complexity $\mathrm{xc}(P)$ is the minimum size of an extended formulation of $P$, equivalently the minimum number of facets of a polytope that affinely projects onto $P$. Known bounds: $\mathrm{xc}(P_{\mathrm{sp.trees}}(G))=O(|V||E|)$ for every connected graph (Wong, Martin), and $O(|V|)$ for connected planar graphs (Williams). A minor-closed family is proper if it does not contain all graphs; the constant in the $O(\cdot)$ may depend on $\mathcal{C}$. This generalizes the authors' conjecture that the bound is linear for graphs embedded in any fixed surface (they prove $O(|V|^{3/2})$ there). The conjecture is known to hold when the graphs in $\mathcal{C}$ have bounded treewidth (Kolman, Koutecký, Tiwary), and the authors prove it for $k$-apex graphs (graphs $G$ with a set $X$ of at most $k$ vertices such that $G-X$ is planar), showing $\mathrm{xc}(P_{\mathrm{sp.trees}}(G))=O(k|E|)=O(k^2|V|)$.
paper_title: Smaller Extended Formulations for the Spanning Tree Polytope of Bounded-genus Graphs
